article_title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
adaptation_summary: Adapted for level C; emphasis on article-specific comprehension, vocabulary in context, and concise written responses.

tasks.prompt: Why were COP31 negotiations in deadlock?
options: Countries disagreed over fossil-fuel language and adaptation finance
The summit venue lost electricity
All Pacific island nations left before talks began
Delegates agreed too quickly on every issue
tasks.correct_answer: Countries disagreed over fossil-fuel language and adaptation finance
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המבוי הסתום נבע בעיקר ממחלוקת על אזכור צמצום דלקי המאובנים ועל מימון הסתגלות למדינות מתפתחות.

tasks.prompt: What could happen if countries fail to reach the consensus required by the UN process?
options: The EU would decide alone
The agreement would automatically become law
The summit could end without a deal and be reconvened next year
Saudi Arabia would host an immediate second vote
tasks.correct_answer: The summit could end without a deal and be reconvened next year
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ללא הסכמה מלאה, השיחות עלולות להסתיים בלי הסכם ולהתכנס מחדש בשנה הבאה.

tasks.prompt: Which group was seeking a stronger commitment on adaptation money?
options: Fossil-fuel producers led by Saudi Arabia
The Africa Group
Only the United States
Cambridge University
tasks.explanation_hebrew: קבוצת אפריקה דרשה התחייבויות חזקות יותר למימון הסתגלות לשינוי האקלים.

tasks.prompt: What does “overshoot” mean in the article's climate context?
options: A sudden increase in airline traffic
A successful reduction below all targets
A financial promise that exceeds $120bn
A period in which global warming rises beyond the 1.5C goal
tasks.correct_answer: A period in which global warming rises beyond the 1.5C goal
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בהקשר הכתבה, overshoot הוא מצב שבו ההתחממות חורגת מיעד 1.5 מעלות.

tasks.prompt: What adaptation-finance figure appeared in earlier drafts but was removed?
options: £1.5bn each year
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בטיוטות מוקדמות נכללה העלאת מימון ההסתגלות ל־120 מיליארד דולר עד 2035, אך המספר הוסר.

tasks.prompt: Why were some delegations changing flights from Sunday to Monday?
options: They wanted an extra holiday in Turkey
The summit had already produced a final deal
They expected negotiations to continue because agreement was not yet in sight
Airlines had banned climate negotiators from flying
tasks.correct_answer: They expected negotiations to continue because agreement was not yet in sight
tasks.explanation_hebrew: שינוי הטיסות מעיד שהמשלחות ציפו להמשך השיחות מפני שהסכם עדיין לא נראה קרוב.

tasks.prompt: Describe the proposed trade-off involving Saudi Arabia and other petro-states.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שההצעה תשאיר את דלקי המאובנים מחוץ לנוסח, ובתמורה מדינות פטרו יתחייבו ש־35% מצריכת האנרגיה שלהן תהיה חשמלית עד 2035.
expected_points: Language on fossil fuels would remain out of the final text.
Saudi Arabia and other petro-states would pledge that 35% of their energy consumption would come from electricity by 2035.

tasks.prompt: Why did Monique Barbut criticise references to carbon capture, use and storage?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר שהיא חששה שהטכנולוגיה תשמש כרישיון להמשיך לשרוף נפט וגז במקום להפחית את השימוש בהם, במיוחד לאחר החמצת יעד 1.5 מעלות.
expected_points: Carbon capture stores emissions underground after they are released.
Barbut feared the references would give countries permission to continue burning oil and gas.
She argued this was inconsistent with acknowledging the severity of exceeding the 1.5C goal.

tasks.prompt: Write 3–4 sentences comparing the positions of Wopke Hoekstra, Miatta Fahnbulleh and Chris Bowen.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג את הוקסטרה כאיום שלא יהיה הסכם בלי פעולה מספקת, את פאהנבולה כאופטימית יותר, ואת בואן כמי שמעדיף התמקדות ביישום ובאנרגיה נקייה במקום אזכור דלקי מאובנים.
expected_points: Hoekstra warned that the EU would reject a deal without sufficient climate action.
Fahnbulleh said difficult but productive talks still left room for agreement.
Bowen argued that the summit should focus on implementation and clean energy rather than explicit fossil-fuel language.
Their positions show different judgments about what the final text must contain.

tasks.prompt: Summarise the COP31 deadlock, the risks of failure and the evidence of change outside the summit in 4–5 sentences.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול את שתי המחלוקות המרכזיות, דרישת הקונצנזוס והסיכון להתכנסות מחדש, וכן את צמיחת האנרגיה המתחדשת ואת המתח מול החלטות להגדיל ייצור נפט.
expected_points: Negotiators were divided over fossil-fuel language and adaptation funding.
Without consensus, the summit could end with no deal and resume the following year.
Delegates leaving could also threaten the number of countries needed to approve an agreement.
Outside COP, solar became the biggest contributor to new global energy demand.
At the same time, major leaders agreed to increase oil production, illustrating conflicting energy trends.
